races.name: Living North Magazines Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over hurdles recently, suggesting retained ability, though 301 days since last flat run creates uncertainty
runners_data.spotlight: Still a maiden on the Flat but a winner over hurdles at Sedgefield for his present yard over the winter so can't be dismissed back in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but pulled up last time over hurdles, needs to bounce back from disappointing Hexham effort
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last August; some good runs over hurdles and on the Flat since; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Resumed winning ways at Wolverhampton (9.5f) in February but he was pulled up back hurdling at Hexham 24 days ago; not out of things if shrugging off that effort.

runners_data.name: Prince Hector
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who wasn't disgraced at Redcar eight days ago, quick return suggests connections are confident
runners_data.comment: 0-14 on turf; tailed off over 1m4f at Catterick last time (lost a shoe); others stronger
runners_data.spotlight: On a long losing run but he wasn't disgraced with sixth of 12 in 1m2f Redcar handicap eight days ago; no forlorn hope.

runners_data.name: Heartened
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course and distance win in September, solid third at Redcar suggests return to form
runners_data.comment: Yet to win on turf; good 3rd at Beverley last June; tailed off last time; plenty to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a first win over C&D in September; got back on track despite not enjoying the smoothest of passages when third of 12 in 1m2f handicap at Redcar eight days ago so she must enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Baldosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old getting weight allowance, step up in trip may help her find improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Remains winless and she comes here on the back a below-par fifth in 1m handicap at Redcar 26 days ago; needs this step up in trip to spark some progress.

runners_data.name: Come On John
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer below par for current stable, 34 days off suggests freshening up attempt
runners_data.comment: Badly out of sorts when last seen in the autumn
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 1m4f scorer for James Owen last March but below par for his current stable, a never-dangerous fourth of seven on his return in 1m1f Musselburgh handicap 34 days ago; needs to take a big step forward.

runners_data.name: Carida
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden who showed little when tenth at Redcar, hood applied suggests trainer seeking improvement
runners_data.comment: Unexposed; tailed off both turf starts, latest at Doncaster last time; stamina to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Modest maiden for Michael Herrington in 2025; yet to show much for her new yard this season, retried in a hood when tenth of 12 in 1m2f Redcar handicap eight days ago; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Crumpet
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form is concerning, course and distance winner but needs significant bounce back
runners_data.comment: Creditable 3rd at Southwell in January; not so good since but wouldn't rule out
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Carlisle (1m) last May but her more recent form is much less encouraging, beating just one in 1m2f Redcar handicap eight days ago; this C&D scorer needs to take a major step forward.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good form with recent wind surgery, strong stayer who handles this distance well
runners_data.comment: Easy win here (1m4f) on his penultimate run and has claims if he can recapture that form
runners_data.spotlight: Back to winning ways at Southwell (1m4f) in March and has continued in good nick, undergoing wind surgery before third of 11 in 1m6f handicap there 33 days ago; very much one to consider in a change of headgear.

runners_data.name: Project Kinsman
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old with warning about fading, getting weight allowance and showed improvement in handicaps
runners_data.comment: Better on her C&D handicap debut here 18 days ago; that gave something to build on
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden who has improved for the recent switch to handicaps, third of eight over C&D last time; she's not taken lightly in this grade with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Broadstone
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer winless in 16 starts, 117 days off after poor February run creates major doubts
runners_data.spotlight: Is 0-16 and he beat only one in 1m4f Southwell handicap in February; needs to bounce back after a break.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse yet to win but solid sixth at Ayr suggests some ability, needs significant improvement at these weights
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to register a victory but he comes here on the back of a solid sixth of 11 in 1m1f handicap at Ayr four weeks ago; more is needed at these weights though if he is to get off the mark.

runners_data.name: Lawmans Blis
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won at Catterick after wind surgery, 22 days between runs suits his rhythm
runners_data.spotlight: Won on his second stable start (and second run since wind surgery) in 14-runner handicap at Catterick (1m4f) last month, getting up late having lost a lot of ground when hampered around half a mile out; big player here.

races.paceDynamic: Lawmans Blis will be the primary pace-setter from his prominent style, with Prince Hector and Wheres The Crumpet likely to race handy early. With only one confirmed front runner, Lawmans Blis can dictate a controlled tempo through the early stages before the race develops in the final three furlongs. The large field of hold-up horses including Yakhabar, Heartened, and Project Kinsman will be relying on pace injection late. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close enough to strike, as the hold-up brigade may struggle to make meaningful inroads from the back in a steadily-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Lawmans Blis dictates an uncontested lead through steady fractions
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get first run on the field while the hold-up horses are left with too much to do from the back. Horses positioned within the first six turning for home will dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Injection Creates Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from the home turn as multiple horses challenge
scenarios.body: The increased gallop sets up perfectly for the stronger stayers with tactical pace who can close from mid-division. Project Kinsman and Yakhabar benefit from their recent good form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains sedate throughout with the real racing saved for the final furlong
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of finishing speed rather than stamina, suiting those with natural acceleration. Heartened's recent third at Redcar suggests retained ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Lawmans Blis faces no serious early pressure and is allowed to coast
scenarios.body: The recent Catterick winner can utilise his stamina advantage over this trip to score from the front. His late-closing style when winning suggests he can quicken when challenged.

watchPoints.text: Project Kinsman carries a specific warning about fading in the finish despite her recent improvement in handicaps
Lawmans Blis faces his first real test since winning at Catterick and must prove he can handle early pressure
Yakhabar underwent wind surgery before his last run, monitor early for any breathing issues affecting his rhythm
Top Flight Century returning after 301 days off the flat creates significant uncertainty about his current ability
Gemini Man was pulled up last time over hurdles at Hexham, watch for any lingering effects from that poor effort

races.name: Living North Christmas Fair Handicap

runners_data.name: Rubellite
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs pace to aim at but has strong recent C&D form and handles this surface well
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Southwell on her stable debut and a bit better than the bare result latest
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Richard Fahey; seven-time AW winner, including two over C&D early last year; off the mark for current trainer at Wolverhampton last time (1m6f; form fair); up 2lb; should go well again.

runners_data.name: Havachoc
runners_data.note: Another closer who completed a hat-trick earlier this year and has solid course form, but needs the race to unfold
runners_data.comment: AW hat-trick this winter and solid in defeat since; solid chance with headgear fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick of wins in January/February, the third off 2lb lower over C&D; has continued in good form and is 2lb better off having been beaten 0.5l by Rubellite at Wolverhampton last time; interesting.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but has been disappointing lately and tends to fade in the finish according to profile
runners_data.comment: Both wins came when trained in France; yet to be placed in 14 starts for current yard.
runners_data.spotlight: Two good C&D runs off higher marks in September/October last year, but disappointing since, including back on turf at Ripon last time.

runners_data.name: Desert Quest
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with C&D winning form who showed signs of a return to form last time at Catterick
runners_data.comment: 8yo who is not easy to fancy on the evidence of this year's two runs
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in January 2024 and several fair efforts after that; ran his best race since a 590-day break when a good fourth at Catterick last time; each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden returning from 272-day break, making this a tough assignment despite fair historical course form
runners_data.comment: Modest handicapper at up to 1m5f on the Flat; best watched after a break on hurdles debut
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden; ran a couple of fair races over 1m2f last year, notably a 2.5l third in a 1m2f handicap here; not done quite as well since and was tailed off in a Kelso novice hurdle nine days ago (not jump well); stamina to prove.

runners_data.name: Ned Broy
runners_data.note: Unexposed hold-up type whose recent second at Hamilton suggests untapped potential over this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed maiden; ran one of his best races on the Flat when coming from off the pace to finish second at Hamilton last time (1m3f, good; 28-1); effective on the AW and interesting with cheekpieces tried.

runners_data.name: Roger Henry
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who could sit handy to Drumcondra but hasn't found form since returning from long absence
runners_data.comment: Back from long absence with a tailed-off effort here (1m) last month; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Wins have been over 7f (AW) and 1m2f (soft); had been off for 570 days before March reappearance (here) and is yet to find his form for this new yard.

runners_data.name: Arch Legend
runners_data.note: Prominent style returning from 301-day layoff, making this a difficult spot despite previous course experience
runners_data.comment: Struggled for this yard last summer and returns from nine months off tonight
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins for Charlie Johnston in 2024, including over 1m4f on Tapeta; mixed form since and may be better for the run after 301-day break; refused to enter stalls on intended reappearance.

runners_data.name: Apache Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden who has been placed in recent similar company and could benefit if the pace sets up right
runners_data.spotlight: 18-race maiden; placed on five occasions, notably when third to Rubellite and Havachoc at Wolverhampton last month (1m6f); each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Drumcondra
runners_data.note: The key pace angle as sole front-runner, though unproven beyond 1m2f and having just second AW start
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden; having only his second run on the AW (fair effort on first occasion) and his first run at beyond 1m2f so has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 225-day break, making this an ambitious comeback assignment
runners_data.comment: Trailed home last in the Chepstow race won by Thewoodcorner; stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 2m at Ffos Las for Jedd O'Keeffe last August (good to soft; awarded race by the stewards) and some fair efforts after that; not done as well since (tailed off over hurdles last time) and has been well beaten all three AW runs; back after wind surgery.

races.paceDynamic: Drumcondra is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a manageable pace over this extended trip. Roger Henry and Arch Legend may sit prominent, but the majority including Rubellite, Havachoc, Desert Quest, and Apache Eagle prefer to come from behind. With minimal early pace pressure, Drumcondra can dictate fractions and kick clear, while the hold-up brigade may find themselves with too much ground to make up on the long home straight. This tactical scenario strongly favours the front-runner and any horse that can travel prominently early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Drumcondra Dictates Terms
scenarios.trigger: If Drumcondra gets away with soft fractions uncontested through the first mile
scenarios.body: He can string out the field and prove hard to peg back, while the hold-up horses struggle to bridge the gap. The front-runner's tactical advantage becomes decisive over this stamina-testing trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely run despite Drumcondra's presence up front
scenarios.body: The closers get their ideal setup with horses coming back to them in the straight. Rubellite and Havachoc can use their proven finishing kicks to maximum effect.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Roger Henry or Arch Legend can sit close enough without overracing
scenarios.body: They get the perfect trip behind the leader and can strike at the optimal moment. Their positioning allows them to respond to any move while avoiding the traffic that troubles the rear division.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Drumcondra stops quickly after dictating and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The better handicapped runners from midfield can capitalize on the tactical chaos. Form and class become more important than running style in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Drumcondra gets any early company from Roger Henry or Arch Legend, which could compromise his tactical advantage
Monitor how quickly the hold-up brigade can get into contention turning for home, as the long straight may not provide enough time
Check if Apache Eagle can improve on his recent third behind Rubellite and Havachoc in similar company
Observe whether Arch Legend shows any ring-rustiness early after his 301-day absence
Watch for any reluctance from Arch Legend to enter the stalls given his previous issues with starting

races.name: Penny Bakery Handicap

runners_data.name: Mystical Land
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good recent course form but 11-race maiden status is concerning against these handicappers
runners_data.comment: Handicapper has given him a chance switched from blinkers to a visor; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden; good run when second over C&D in January; hasn't run quite as well since, although fair run with today's headgear on for first time over C&D two weeks ago (just behind stable companion Golden Havana); each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Star Noir
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this tactical setup and carries highest official rating, though 29 days since last run could blunt sharpness
runners_data.comment: In the frame all five starts in 2025, best run when 2nd in 5f novice; lacks a recent run
runners_data.spotlight: In the frame on all five starts last season, including when fourth on handicap debut over C&D on final outing (2-1 favourite); pulled hard when below-par on Beverley reappearance (5f, good to soft) but should come on for the run; interesting down in grade.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner who benefits from retaining the visor that aided his victory here in November
runners_data.comment: Course regular whose latest fourth here has been boosted since; decent claims
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner off 3lb higher in November when blinkered for first time; creditable runs over C&D on last two starts (tried in a visor, which is retained, last time); a possible.

runners_data.name: Dontwaste A Moment
runners_data.note: Lone front runner drops back to 5f for first time which may suit his tactical style better than longer trips
runners_data.comment: Just modest form in three runs over 6f; AW/handicap debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form in 6f turf novice/maidens last season; well beaten on handicap debut at Wolverhampton when stepped up to 7f on reappearance; first run at 5f.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces difficult task with so many prominent runners likely to dominate early positioning
runners_data.comment: 6f AW win last month before finding 5f too sharp latest; still in form; each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner over 6f in April; sound run when fourth over 5f at Musselburgh next time; still feasibly treated; interesting.

runners_data.name: Master Harry
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 179-day absence with tongue-tie fitted for first time, making fitness and breathing aids key factors
runners_data.comment: Beat one in 5f nursery here 13 days ago; tongue-tie is reached for now with a bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Mixed efforts for Ann Duffield last season, his best effort when third in a C&D novice in September; very well handicapped on that form, and having since been gelded and given a wind op, is one with a chance; cheekpieces now tried.

races.paceDynamic: Dontwaste A Moment is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the rail, likely setting a measured gallop without early pressure. Star Noir, Mystical Land, Golden Havana and Master Harry all show prominent tendencies and will track close behind in the first three furlongs. With five of six runners preferring to race up with the pace and only Pivotal Terms showing hold-up instincts, this creates a bunched field through halfway before a sprint finish develops. The tactical verdict strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can secure early position, as the lone hold-up horse Pivotal Terms faces an almost impossible task from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dontwaste Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Dontwaste A Moment gets an uncontested lead and the prominent horses settle behind him
scenarios.body: The pace-setter kicks for home at the two-furlong pole and the prominent trackers respond, creating a sustained drive that suits horses with tactical speed. Golden Havana and Star Noir benefit from their proven course form and prominent styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If two or more of the prominent runners press Dontwaste A Moment early and create stronger tempo
scenarios.body: The increased gallop stretches the field and sets up a finishing kick scenario where class and proven ability at the trip becomes decisive. Star Noir's superior rating and Golden Havana's course-winning form prove crucial in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady to Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Dontwaste A Moment sets a pedestrian pace and the field stays compact into the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the two-furlong marker where horses with the best recent form and tactical positioning dominate. Mystical Land's good recent course run and Golden Havana's proven 5f speed come to the fore.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too fast early and compromise each other in a speed duel
scenarios.body: Pivotal Terms gets the perfect setup from his hold-up position as the pace collapses, allowing him to use his proven course form and 5f ability. The front-runners tie up and the race falls to the patient hold-up runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Dontwaste A Moment gets pressured early by Star Noir or Golden Havana, as this could compromise the front runner's stamina reserves
Monitor Pivotal Terms' early positioning as he needs the prominent runners to go too fast to have any realistic winning chance
Observe Master Harry's jumping and early pace after his long layoff, as 179 days absence could show in his initial sharpness
Check if Mystical Land can translate his recent course placings into a breakthrough win against stronger handicap opposition
Watch for Golden Havana to travel smoothly in his retained visor, as this headgear change coincided with his course victory

races.name: Penny On The Move Handicap

runners_data.name: Let's Go Hugo
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with dual C&D wins but mixed recent form and quick return after seven days
runners_data.comment: All wins at 5f and he was only tenth over C&D recently, finishing behind two of these
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D winner, latest victory last September; mixed form since; wouldn't rule out.

runners_data.name: What What What
runners_data.note: Pure closer with C&D win and February success, perfectly suited to weak pace after 33-day break
runners_data.comment: C&D win in February; struggled, not for the first time on turf, 12 days ago; can rebound
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner last year; won again at Southwell in February (6f) but rather out of sorts since; back on his last winning mark.

runners_data.name: Desert Champion
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who fades late, likely pace-setter but vulnerable to closers in final furlong
runners_data.comment: On a reduced mark but it is easy enough to have reservations for now
runners_data.spotlight: Only win was a 5f handicap at Chelmsford in March 2025 when visored for the first time; would have a chance on his C&D second off 8lb higher last November, but below-par recently; no visor this time.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with C&D win in visor, strong recent second suggests returning to form
runners_data.comment: 3lb lower than when fourth at Doncaster on penultimate start; possibilities on that form
runners_data.spotlight: Only win was over C&D in March when wearing a visor for the first time; best run since when second at Redcar last week (5f, good to firm); chance.

runners_data.name: Jeany May
runners_data.note: Prominent style with visor fitted after decent Redcar fourth, needs to find improvement
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy having not beaten many in three starts since returning last month; visor on
runners_data.spotlight: Ran two good races on AW last year; best form this year when fourth at Redcar last week (5f, good to firm; visor first time); has a bit to find with runner-up Auntie Jo on that run, but her stable is in fine form at present.

runners_data.name: Posh Maisie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie after 386 days off, best watched on return
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some fair form in Ireland in her younger days, but has proved disappointing and is best watched after 386 days off.

runners_data.name: A Lady Forever
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in visor with C&D win for previous yard, moderate form this season
runners_data.comment: Sole win in weak 0-50 classified at Newcastle in February 2025; 0-14 since; look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 6f here in February 2025 for Roger Fell when returning from a long break; has shown bits of form since, but not been at  her best this year.

runners_data.name: Bishop's Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with C&D form wearing visor, 124 days off raises fitness questions
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 6f here in November; plenty of sound placed efforts since (beaten a head over C&D in January) and could go well if fit after a break.

runners_data.name: Hyrcanian
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden who fades late, poor recent form suggests others stronger
runners_data.comment: 15-race maiden and didn't run well enough at Catterick after her break
runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden; hasn't shown much in her two runs this year; others look stronger

runners_data.name: Barney's Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in visor trying 5f for first time since 2024, 52-day break
runners_data.spotlight: 1-34 on the AW, that win coming over 6f at Southwell in April 2021; rather out of sorts over 6f-1m this year and now tries 5f for the first time since May 2024.

races.paceDynamic: Desert Champion is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the rail with minimal pressure early. Jeany May and A Lady Forever may track him in second and third, but both have prominent rather than pure pace-setting styles. This creates a controlled tempo over 5f with Desert Champion building a soft lead before the field closes from halfway. The lack of genuine pace pressure favours horses that can settle and produce a late kick rather than those needing to race prominently.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Champion sets an uncontested lead with gentle fractions
scenarios.body: The pace collapses in the final furlong as hold-up horses unleash superior finishing kicks. What What What and Auntie Jo benefit most from the tactical setup with their proven closing ability at the trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Desert Champion Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Champion maintains his lead under minimal pressure throughout
scenarios.body: His sustainable gallop proves enough as the closers leave their runs too late on the sharp 5f trip. Jeany May and A Lady Forever pick up the pieces as the best-placed stalkers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If Jeany May or A Lady Forever press Desert Champion from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates gaps for horses with turn-of-foot. Bishop's Glory and Auntie Jo benefit from the honest pace that sets up their finishing kicks perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Champion fades early leaving a pace vacuum
scenarios.body: The race becomes scrappy with no clear leader, favouring horses that can adapt tactically. A Lady Forever and Jeany May can press forward while What What What struggles to find racing room in the melee.

watchPoints.text: Desert Champion could steal this if allowed completely uncontested fractions and the closers are too far back
Bishop's Glory fitness after 124 days off - needs to be monitored in preliminaries for signs of readiness
What What What may need the run after 33 days off despite strong form when fresh
Jeany May first-time visor could spark improvement after moderate recent efforts
Track conditions favoring front runners would significantly boost Desert Champion's chances

races.name: Penny Car Washes Handicap

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly placed for this pace shape, strong recent Hamilton form suggests current wellbeing
runners_data.comment: Off eight months, winning start for new yard here latest; not taken lightly under 5lb pen
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning stable debut at Hamilton (8.5f; 20-1) last month; backed that up, splitting a Jim Goldie pair (third has won since), under a 5lb penalty there (1m1f) next time; 1lb lower now and has no issues with this AW track (311224); interesting.

runners_data.name: Criminal Shore
runners_data.note: Prominent runner facing traffic danger, David O'Meara strike-rate concerning at 2/48 over 14 days
runners_data.comment: Rare run at shy of 1m when not far behind three of these over C&D last month; consistent
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 19 came at Ripon (1m, good) last April; mostly consistent this year, a close fourth to Flying Fletcher over C&D in January, and occupied that same position behind Barry's Boy here in March; easing mark, with Paul Mulrennan booked for the first time.

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but slow starts problematic, apprentice Ethan Tindall may struggle in traffic
runners_data.comment: Ended long losing run at Newcastle in January and largely in good form since; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Best RPRs over shorter (6f) but did make all in a slowly run C&D Class 4 in January (4-1); failed to get majorly competitive - often slowly away - in his last three starts; return to AW might assist, along with Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Prominent style risky in this field configuration, 34 days off after non-runner suggests issues
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with reappearance win at Southwell; remains on workable mark back up 4lb
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of an easing mark to make a winning seasonal reappearance at Southwell (1m; 14-1, first start since wind surgery) in late April; non-runner at Thirsk (ground) on Sunday, and this looks a better fit; likely to have a say from 4lb higher.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with excellent recent form, perfect profile for this pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Chased home the bang-in-form Aisling Oscar over C&D in December, and he's 2-2 since returning from a break, winning at Southwell and Thirsk (both 1m); has risen a combined total of 10lb (3lb since latest) for those two wins, but he has to figure on the shortlist in pursuit of the hat-trick.

runners_data.name: Chuzzlewit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on attractive mark but 38-day break concerning, rarely wins despite ability
runners_data.comment: Regressive 6yo who finished well down the field on last month's turf return
runners_data.spotlight: Fine looker, and for all that he's an infrequent winner (2-35), was once rated in the 90s; placed in a Class 4 over C&D (from 10lb higher) last June but he's been steadily regressive since; safer options elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Cusack
runners_data.note: Prominent runner well-handicapped, Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim valuable but faces traffic
runners_data.comment: 50-1 for his C&D return, when well behind a few of these, and needs a big step forward
runners_data.spotlight: 10-47 on AW, with all bar one of those wins coming at Newcastle (7f-1m2f); now sits 3lb below his last winning mark, and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is a bonus, but seems to have lost his way; may strip fitter for 7f course comeback run.

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader ideally positioned, poor recent form offset by tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Well held at long odds for this yard; probably best watched unless strong in the market
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times in Ireland for Mick Mulvany, including at Listowel (1m, heavy) last September; low key in five starts for new trainer, slipping 9lb in the weights - now 1lb below that last winning mark; needs revival on AW return (3-9).

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good course form but hung left under pressure last time
runners_data.comment: Won at Newcastle in March and he's only 3lb higher after another break; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on well to justify favouritism over C&D (from 3lb lower) on penultimate start; beaten - fifth, hung left under pressure - in a stronger Class 4 at Nottingham subsequently; might have to settle for minor honours on AW return.

runners_data.name: American State
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits race shape, 37-day gap since Wolverhampton run needs monitoring
runners_data.comment: Hard to predict but he's won twice on AW this year and still looks on a workable mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice this year (post wind surgery) for Ivan Furtado, keeping on well at Southwell (1m, Class 5; from 4lb lower) on penultimate start; not at his best at Wetherby (tenth) latest, but there's still a chance he can prove competitive from this revised mark.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with five course wins but slow starts recently problematic
runners_data.spotlight: Five C&D wins, the latest from a 3lb lower mark in December; has struggled at double-figure odds on turf lately (Musselburgh and Hamilton) with slow starts a regular feature; drops back into a Class 5 now at a more suitable track, but with enough to prove for the time being.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Prominent runner dropping significantly in grade, Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helpful
runners_data.comment: In good form last May-July; player if he can stay 1m2f, which isn't nailed on
runners_data.spotlight: In fine fettle (form figure 522122) last spring/summer, rounding off with a close second to Eeetee at Redcar (1m, good to soft, 6-4 favourite) in July; fair sixth to Military Leader on Southwell comeback run but disappointed over 1m2f at Haydock subsequently; best watched.

races.paceDynamic: Sunriseontheboyne will lead uncontested from the break, setting a steady gallop without early pressure. Criminal Shore, Alessia Fernanda, Barry's Boy, Cusack and Bellasio will cluster prominently behind, creating congestion tracking the leader. The prominent pack will jostle for position approaching the home turn, while hold-up horses Quiet Resolve, Flying Fletcher, Military Leader, Chuzzlewit, American State and Second Fiddle must navigate traffic from the rear. This moderate early pace followed by prominent congestion 2-3 furlongs out clearly favours the lone leader and patient hold-up horses who can find clear runs late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Soft Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Sunriseontheboyne sets uncontested fractions and the prominent pack marks each other.
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage while the clustered prominents neutralise each other's kicks. Sunriseontheboyne capitalises on the tactical advantage while one hold-up horse finds the clearest late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates a wall of horses turning for home.
scenarios.body: The bunched prominents block each other while patient hold-up runners sweep wide with clear runs. Military Leader or Quiet Resolve time their challenges perfectly as the pace collapses ahead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners avoids the traffic and kicks clear 2f out.
scenarios.body: Barry's Boy or Criminal Shore finds racing room before the others and exploits their class edge. The leader ties up while other prominents remain trapped behind the early pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Scramble Finish
scenarios.trigger: If severe traffic problems affect most runners and the pace completely collapses.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses are denied clear runs creating a lottery finish where any horse finding daylight can win. An outsider like Cusack or Chuzzlewit could capitalise on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Criminal Shore, Barry's Boy and Cusack will create a prominent traffic jam 2-3 furlongs out
Second Fiddle and Flying Fletcher both prone to slow starts which could prove costly
Military Leader has the perfect hold-up profile if finding clear racing room late
Sunriseontheboyne sets the pace but recent form figures suggest vulnerability if pressed
Quiet Resolve's recent winning form at Hamilton suggests current wellbeing for patient tactics

races.name: Penny Hotels Handicap

runners_data.name: Barleybrown
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong C&D record when getting right trip, 16 days since last run freshens him up
runners_data.comment: Won four times on Newcastle AW in 2024 but winless since.
runners_data.spotlight: Won four over C&D (BHA marks between 50-60) in 2024; began 2026 with a respectable third to Sea Legend, but it's been disappointing - with some mitigation - that he hasn't built on that since; stablemate of Billyjoegold.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse who ran well here in December, but recent Ripon effort suggests declining form
runners_data.comment: Has three course wins over 1m2f; hasn't figured since returning to turf last month.
runners_data.spotlight: 9-96; just failed to reel in Wyvern over 7f here in December but laboured since; weakened, well down the field at Ripon (1m, good; beaten 17l) latest; is fairly treated but the chances are that age is beginning to catch up with him.

runners_data.name: Mercurius Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up type now 7lb lower than last win, Jessica Macey struggling for winners with 0/10 record past 14 days
runners_data.comment: It's now 17 outings since last success; easing in the weights though and no forlorn hope
runners_data.spotlight: Difficult to win with in recent years, now 7lb lower than when last successful at Southwell (1m) in August 2024; met trouble when sixth (beaten over 4l) here on penultimate start, but latest Leicester effort was less encouraging.

runners_data.name: First Encounter
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner gives him tactical advantage, 64 days freshened up after decent classified wins earlier
runners_data.comment: Made the most of the drop to classified level, winning 2-3 this year; more needed today
runners_data.spotlight: Hit form, winning classified contests at Wolverhampton (8.5f) and Lingfield (1m) earlier this year; not far off those levels when last seen at Wolverhampton (sixth) two months ago; possible player on first visit to Newcastle with the promising Conor Whiteley booked.

runners_data.name: Trais Fluors
runners_data.note: 12-year-old hold-up horse with solid C&D form but limited winning opportunities at this stage of career
runners_data.comment: 12yo who wasn't beaten far at Ayr latest but his last turf win was almost three years ago
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran (13-102); has won just once since late 2024, when edging out Pallas Lord over C&D (15-2) on New Year's Day; kept on after a slow start, fifth of seven, at Ayr (7f; 33-1) four weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Cable Beach
runners_data.note: Hold-up type freshened by 133-day break, showed ability when winning at Southwell last November
runners_data.spotlight: Pounced late at Southwell (7f; from 2lb lower) last November and close up (fourth) behind Little Ted over 7f here the following month; freshened up since fair third at Southwell (first try at 1m) in January; market can guide.

runners_data.name: Penny Mountain
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with good recent Newcastle form including 6f win here, step up to 1m may suit
runners_data.spotlight: Ready winner here (6f, Class 6; 11-1) on New Year's Day, and in the frame four times since, including over 7f here (18-1) in March; fifth at Musselburgh latest and that form has taken a few knocks since; tackles 1m for the first time.

runners_data.name: Volenti
runners_data.note: Four C&D wins suggests track specialist, but Ben Haslam's poor 0/14 record raises trainer form concerns
runners_data.comment: Has four wins on Newcastle AW but is only 1-19 on turf.
runners_data.spotlight: Four C&D wins, including when justifying favouritism in January 2025; in reasonable form on turf this time last year (from marks in mid 60s) but has lost his way since then, tumbling down the handicap; latest Ripon fourth (beaten 8l) isn't enough to tempt.

runners_data.name: Rocket Rod
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from long lay-off with poor recent form, makes no appeal despite easier mark
runners_data.comment: Returned after long absence with two heavy defeats on AW this spring; cheekpieces back on
runners_data.spotlight: 4-39, three of those wins here (7f-1m) in 2022; soundly beaten both starts since returning from a near two-year absence; makes no appeal despite this easing mark.

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won well here in March but bombed out badly next time at Nottingham
runners_data.comment: Remote last on turf latest but pulled hard; ought to fare better back on Tapeta
runners_data.spotlight: Seemed to have turned a corner when cosily accounting for Alpine Sierra (three wins since) over 1m2f here (7-1) in March; bombed out at Nottingham (1m2f) next time and trapped wide at Wolverhampton (9.5f) latest; noted with Jack Garritty (1-2) back aboard.

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.comment: Ex-Gemma Tutty; bought 4,500gns in October and gelded; well beaten on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice for Gemma Tutty, including by a short-head here (7f) in January 2025; changed hands for 4,500gns and is yet to threaten in two starts since a gelding operation; fairly weighted, particularly with Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim to factor in.

runners_data.name: Abu Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type in freefall since joining current trainer, 0/7 record suggests significant problems
runners_data.comment: Long time since sole success; chance depends on how well he reacts to visor
runners_data.spotlight: 1-25, that win for the Johnstons in an Ayr maiden (1m) in May 2023; in freefall since joining this trainer (0-7), weakening tamely after taking a keen hold in an added visor at Southwell (1m3f; last of ten) nine weeks ago, the drop back in trip needs to make a big difference.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose sole win came in heavy ground, struggling on better surfaces this season
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 12 came in the mud at Ffos Las (1m, heavy) last September; didn't offer much in her first three starts this year, and only a smidgen more when sixth of nine at Kempton (1m; 28-1, beaten 3l) four weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Billyjoegold
runners_data.note: Hold-up type still learning his trade, distant third on debut here suggests more needed
runners_data.comment: Bit of promise on debut before two poor efforts; would want to see some support
runners_data.spotlight: Distant third on debut here (7f novice; 66-1) in March and he has struggled in three subsequent appearances; it's still early days and his half-brother Bobby Joe Leg is a prolific winner; stablemate of Barleybrown.

races.paceDynamic: First Encounter looks the sole confirmed early pace and his prominent style should see him dictate from the front without significant pressure. With 13 hold-up horses behind him, this creates a tactical race where the tempo could be modest through the early stages. The lack of genuine pace pressure means First Encounter can control fractions and potentially steal a march, while the massed ranks of hold-up horses will need the pace to develop sufficiently to give them something to aim at. This race shape clearly favours horses with early speed or those that can track the pace prominently, rather than the pure hold-up brigade who may find themselves with too much to do.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals March
scenarios.trigger: If First Encounter gets soft fractions uncontested early
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to build an unassailable lead turning for home, with hold-up horses left flat-footed too far back. His recent form suggests he's capable at this level when getting his own way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and bunches the field
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses with the strongest finishing kicks can overcome the tactical disadvantage and sweep past a weakening leader. Superior class tells in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Injection
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses moves earlier to inject pace
scenarios.body: This creates a more honest gallop that brings stamina into play and sets up a genuine test where the best stayers can prevail. The early leader may crack under increased pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Interference
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of hold-up horses causes traffic problems in the straight
scenarios.body: Navigation becomes crucial and those with clear runs or drawn well have significant advantages over better horses caught in trouble. Experience and jockey skill become paramount.

watchPoints.text: First Encounter breaking clear early if uncontested - his recent wins show he can sustain a lead when getting soft fractions
Traffic problems in straight with 13 hold-up horses all needing room - those drawn wide may have clearer passage
Mercurius Power and Penny Mountain both dropping significantly in grade and could outclass these if race develops right
Jockey inexperience with Conor Whiteley (7lb claimer) on the likely pace-setter potentially affecting tactical execution
Cable Beach returning from long absence could be sharper than recent form suggests given his previous course ability
